newsitem.title: BULGARIA: INSTANT VIEW - BULGARIA MAY INFLATION RISES TO 5.6 PCT.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - BULGARIA MAY INFLATION RISES TO 5.6 PCT.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on Bulgaria May inflation quickening to 5.6 percent after falling 0.7 percent in April.

PARVOLETA SHTEREVA, EMERGING MARKETS ECONOMIST ING BANK LONDON - Our May inflation estimate was around of six percent. We see consistant lowering of the monthly inflation rate with the introduction of the currency board and the government trying to achieve IMF tragets of two percent monthly by the end of the year.

The June inflation could be moderately high with the slight devaluotion of the lev, being fixed to the German mark at 1,000. But I expect inflation to start dropping sharply from July, partly because food prices, which form a big part of the basket, fall in this season.

FRANK KOHLENBERGER, RESEARCH ECONOMIST, MMS INTERNATIONAL ANALYTICAL SERVICE, LONDON - It is a moderate figure compared to the hyperinflation in the beginning of the year. We still have a decline compared to March and April. I think the positive trend is still underlying even if it is higher than what the government expected.

KAMEN KOLCHEV, MANAGER, ELANA FINANCIAL COMPANY, SOFIA - The major inflation boosting factor is the electricity rate hike in April which has long-term effect on production cycles. I see inflation in June around three to five percent due to the slight devaluation of the lev after being fixed to the mark. If there are no further electricity or fuel price rises, we can expect inflation in July and August to slow to around zero.
